overview: Baker Hughes is a global energy and industrial technology company that provides equipment, technology, and services across the full energy value chain, from oil and gas well construction and production to gas turbines, compression, industrial power systems, and now cryogenic/thermal management equipment. Following the $13.6 billion (~$14.2 billion cash paid) acquisition of Chart Industries, which closed July 16, 2026, the company now reports three segments -- Oilfield Services & Equipment (OFSE), Industrial & Energy Technology (IET), and Chart -- and operates in more than 120 countries. Customers span national and international oil companies, LNG developers, industrial gas and manufacturing customers, utilities, and a fast-growing base of data center/AI infrastructure developers.

business_model.summary: OFSE (oilfield services and equipment tied to drilling, completions, production, and subsea) is now roughly 48% of revenue and remains the more transactional, oil-price-cyclical business. IET (gas technology/turbomachinery, industrial technology, and new energy/climate solutions) is roughly 40% of revenue, with large multi-year order backlogs ($39.4B record IET remaining performance obligations at Q3 2026) and growing recurring aftermarket/service revenue. Chart, consolidated since mid-July 2026, contributed $888 million of revenue in its first full reporting quarter (Q3 2026) -- about 11% of total revenue -- split between original equipment (~70%) and aftermarket (~30%), and management guides Chart segment EBITDA margin toward 22-23% by H2 2028 as integration and cost synergies ($325M annualized target, with $70M already executed) ramp.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - national and international oil companies, LNG developers/operators, industrial gas and manufacturing customers, data center/power infrastructure developers (incl. a 1.1 GW integrated power order for a major US technology company), and utilities
business_model.geographic_mix: Global operations across North America, Middle East, Asia Pacific, Europe, Latin America, and Africa; Middle East and Asia remain central to OFSE/IET growth strategy, with meaningful exposure to Saudi Aramco and other Gulf national oil companies; Chart adds a more North America/industrial-gas-weighted revenue base

main_competitors: Chart's former standalone peers: Linde/Air Products engineering divisions, Cryoworks, Wessington Cryogenics (cryogenic equipment)
competitive_position.market_position: Second-largest oilfield services company by revenue (behind SLB) in the 'Big Three' OFS oligopoly with SLB and Halliburton; holds a dominant, near-monopoly position (~90% share) in turbomachinery for LNG liquefaction via GE-heritage Frame 7/Frame 9 turbines; Chart adds a leading position in cryogenic equipment, heat exchangers, and engineered gas/LNG processing systems used across LNG, hydrogen, and industrial gas value chains

moat_factors.description: Near-90% share of large-scale LNG liquefaction turbomachinery; Frame 7/Frame 9 turbines are the de facto industry standard, creating high switching costs and long-cycle aftermarket service revenue; reinforced by a new Venture Global Plaquemines expansion award covering four liquefaction blocks

Large global installed base of equipment (subsea trees, turbomachinery, compression, and now Chart's cryogenic systems) generates recurring, high-margin services and parts revenue over decades-long equipment life

GE heritage gives deep rotating equipment and turbomachinery engineering expertise, now complemented by Chart's cryogenic/thermal management and brazed aluminum heat exchanger IP, expanding the addressable market to over $400B

moat_factors.factor: Diversified portfolio vs. pure-play OFS peers
moat_factors.description: IET and Chart provide exposure to LNG, power generation, data centers, hydrogen, and industrial gas that SLB and Halliburton largely lack, reducing pure oil-price cyclicality
Operations in 120+ countries support large, complex international and offshore projects that smaller competitors cannot service

weaknesses: OFSE remains exposed to oil price cycles and NOC/IOC capex discipline, including continuing pressure on Saudi Aramco and other national oil company spending
Competes with Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries in turbomachinery, which continue to win select LNG contracts
Significant integration risk and execution burden from the large Chart Industries acquisition, now consolidated with leverage well above historical norms
Chart segment margins (~17.6% EBITDA margin in Q3 2026) are currently below BKR's targeted 22-23% long-term range, requiring multi-year execution to reach
OFSE segment margins remain lower and more volatile than IET margins

growth_drivers: LNG buildout: continued global liquefaction capacity additions favor Baker Hughes' dominant turbomachinery position, with LNG equipment orders targeted to approach $10B over Horizon 2 (2026-2028) and new awards such as Venture Global Plaquemines

AI data center power demand: gas turbine and integrated power orders, including a 1.1 GW order for a major US technology company and ~500MW for a US energy company's AI infrastructure; year-to-date 2026 data center awards reached $4.9B
New Energy portfolio (hydrogen, CCUS, geothermal, emissions management, electrification): revenue has scaled from a few hundred million in 2022 to a multi-billion dollar run rate

Chart Industries integration: expands addressable market to more than $400B, adds cryogenic/thermal management and recurring aftermarket revenue; targeting $325M in annualized cost synergies by year three ($70M already executed) and Chart segment EBITDA margin expansion to 22-23% by H2 2028

Record order backlog: total remaining performance obligations of $46.4B at Q3 2026, including record IET RPO of $39.4B; full-year 2026 IET order guidance raised to $21.5-23.5B and Horizon 2 (2026-2028) IET order outlook raised to more than $50B
Deleveraging path: management targets net leverage below 1.5x by H2 2028, supported by free cash flow generation and continued portfolio simplification/divestitures
International and offshore OFSE project pipeline, including FPSO awards and subsea/gas infrastructure

business.description: OFSE demand is directly tied to customer E&P spending, which fluctuates with oil and gas prices
Pressure on Saudi Aramco and other national oil company capital budgets continues to affect OFSE order timing
Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries continue to compete for LNG and turbine contracts, a long-term threat to BKR's historical dominance

IET and Chart revenue recognition lags bookings by multiple years (CFO noted only ~33% of combined Gas Technology Equipment/Climate Technology Solutions backlog converts in 2027), making near-term results sensitive to project timing and cancellations

Realizing $325M of targeted cost synergies and lifting Chart EBITDA margins from ~17.6% to a 22-23% target by H2 2028 requires sustained management focus; shortfalls would pressure the investment thesis for the deal

financial.risk: Materially increased leverage from Chart acquisition
financial.description: Total debt roughly tripled from ~$6.1B at FY2025 to ~$18.3B at Q3 2026 (long-term debt ~$17.5B, cash ~$4.1B) after BKR paid ~$14.2B cash for Chart; leverage ratio stood at roughly 2.5x at quarter-end against a management target of below 1.5x net leverage by H2 2028, leaving limited room for execution missteps or a downturn

S&P Global downgraded Baker Hughes' issuer rating from A to A- around the Chart deal announcement, reflecting the aggressive initial acquisition financing, even as the company reiterated its commitment to an A-category rating over time
Significant international revenue creates exposure to currency fluctuations in emerging markets
Large equipment and project-based businesses require substantial working capital management

regulatory.description: Evolving emissions regulations affect both traditional oilfield operations and new energy investment economics (CCUS, hydrogen incentives)
Operations in Russia, Middle East, and other geopolitically sensitive regions expose the company to sanctions risk and compliance costs
The Chart deal has closed, but post-closing integration and any required divestitures from regulatory conditions could still affect realized synergies

macro.description: Middle East conflicts (including Houthi attacks affecting Saudi supply routes), Russia-Ukraine war, and other conflicts create supply chain, demand, and safety risks; a 'war premium' in the stock appears to have partly faded in late 2026, contributing to share price weakness

macro.risk: Global economic slowdown / AI capex sentiment shift
macro.description: A recession or a reversal in AI/data center capex sentiment (cited as a factor in the early-November 2026 sell-off across energy and industrial names) would reduce order flow for both traditional energy and data-center-power-linked revenue

macro.risk: Interest rate and financing cost sensitivity
macro.description: Higher-for-longer rates raise financing costs for both customers' capital projects (LNG trains, power plants, data centers) and for BKR's own enlarged, Chart-related debt load
Slower-than-expected new energy adoption or policy reversals (e.g., reduced government support for hydrogen/CCUS) could dampen New Energy segment growth

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management continues to describe an 'energy demand decade' driven by rising global energy consumption, LNG capacity expansion, AI/data center power needs, and continued oil and gas infrastructure investment alongside growing low-carbon/CCUS and industrial gas spend
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate to high for OFSE (tied to oil/gas capex cycles); more moderate for IET and Chart given long-cycle LNG/power/industrial-gas projects and growing recurring services revenue, providing some counter-cyclical balance, though all segments remain sensitive to a broader industrial capex slowdown
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate to high - large customer capital projects (LNG, power, data centers, industrial gas) and BKR's own now much larger debt load (post-Chart, ~$18.3B total debt, ~2.5x leverage) are sensitive to financing costs and credit spreads
key_input_costs: Steel, specialty metals and aluminum (brazed heat exchangers)

recent_developments.event: Reported Q3 2026 results, its first full quarter consolidating Chart: revenue of $8.0B (+14% YoY, ~2% organic ex-Chart), adjusted EBITDA of $1.415B (17.6% margin), adjusted diluted EPS of $0.70 vs. GAAP diluted EPS of $0.41 (profit down ~33% YoY on acquisition-related costs); free cash flow of $769M including ~$200M of Chart integration/restructuring/closing costs

Chart segment contributed $888M of revenue ($623M equipment, $265M aftermarket) and $156M segment EBITDA (~17.6% margin) in its first reporting quarter; management reiterated a 22-23% Chart EBITDA margin target by H2 2028 and said $70M of the $325M targeted annualized cost synergies had already been executed

IET orders rose 42% YoY to $5.89B with record remaining performance obligations of $39.4B; raised full-year 2026 IET order guidance to $21.5-23.5B and Horizon 2 (2026-2028) IET order outlook to more than $50B; year-to-date 2026 data center awards reached $4.9B, including a 1.1GW integrated power order for a major US technology company
Raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue to roughly $29.2-30.1B and adjusted EBITDA to roughly $5.13-5.4B, reflecting the Chart contribution and continued IET/data center momentum

Total debt rose to roughly $18.3B (long-term debt ~$17.5B, cash ~$4.1B) from ~$6.1B at FY2025 year-end, after BKR paid ~$14.2B in cash for Chart; leverage ratio stood at ~2.5x, against a management target of below 1.5x net leverage by H2 2028

Completed the Chart Industries acquisition ($210/share, ~$13.6B enterprise value / ~$14.2B cash paid), adding cryogenic and thermal management capabilities as a new third operating segment ("Chart") alongside OFSE and IET

S&P Global downgraded Baker Hughes' issuer credit rating from A to A- around the Chart deal, citing aggressive initial acquisition financing, even as the company reiterated a long-term commitment to an A-category rating

Stock fell sharply (down ~5-7% over consecutive sessions, trading near $46-48) amid a broader AI-sentiment-driven sell-off in energy/industrial names, a fading geopolitical 'war premium,' and a UBS price target cut to $70 from $71; shares are well off their 2026 highs near $57-60 reached after the Q2 2026 report
Prior to Chart's consolidation, reported record quarterly results (adjusted EPS $0.64, revenue $6.74B) with IET bookings doubling YoY to $7.1B and backlog up 19% to an all-time high at the time

Raised from the prior ~$4.85B guide; includes Chart segment EBITDA of roughly $325-375M for the stub period since close

Raised from the prior $17.5-19.5B guide on record bookings in LNG, power systems, and data-center-related orders; includes ~$18B booked year-to-date through Q3

Versus a reported ~2.5x leverage ratio at Q3 2026 quarter-end following the Chart acquisition financing

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Lorenzo Simonelli continued to characterize the environment as an 'energy demand decade,' citing LNG capacity additions, data center/AI power demand, and industrial gas growth as durable tailwinds, while emphasizing record order backlog ($46.4B total RPO, including $39.4B in IET) as evidence of multi-year revenue visibility. Management acknowledged the step-change in leverage from the Chart acquisition (total debt up to ~$18.3B, leverage near 2.5x) and laid out a deleveraging path to below 1.5x net leverage by H2 2028, alongside a Chart margin-expansion roadmap to 22-23% EBITDA margin over the same horizon, framing integration execution and free cash flow generation as the primary near-term priorities.

bull_case: Near-monopoly position in LNG turbomachinery (~90% share) plus Chart's cryogenic/heat-exchanger technology position Baker Hughes to capture a multi-year global LNG capacity build-out, reinforced by awards like Venture Global Plaquemines

AI data center power demand is a fast-growing, largely oil-price-uncorrelated order stream -- $4.9B of data center awards year-to-date in 2026, including a 1.1GW order for a major technology company -- supporting record IET backlog ($39.4B RPO)

Chart Industries integration expands the addressable market to over $400B and adds recurring cryogenic/thermal aftermarket revenue, with a credible path to 22-23% segment EBITDA margins by H2 2028 and $325M of annualized cost synergies ($70M already executed)
Raised FY2026 guidance (revenue to ~$29.2-30.1B, adjusted EBITDA to ~$5.13-5.4B) and a raised Horizon 2 IET order outlook (>$50B) signal continued momentum independent of near-term integration noise

Recent share price weakness (down from ~$57-60 highs to the mid-$40s on broad AI-sentiment and sector rotation rather than company-specific news) may offer a more attractive entry point relative to the underlying order and backlog trends
bear_case: Leverage has risen sharply from the Chart deal -- total debt roughly tripled to ~$18.3B and leverage near 2.5x, well above the company's own below-1.5x target -- leaving less balance-sheet flexibility and contributing to an S&P downgrade to A-

Chart segment margins (~17.6%) are well below the long-term 22-23% target, and realizing $325M of cost synergies plus margin expansion by H2 2028 requires several more years of flawless integration execution

OFSE remains exposed to oil price volatility and NOC capex discipline (Saudi Aramco and peers), and GAAP profit fell ~33% YoY in Q3 2026 even as adjusted results beat, reflecting real acquisition-related costs (~$200M of integration/restructuring cash costs in the quarter alone)

Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries continue to compete for LNG/turbomachinery contracts, and a reversal in AI/data-center capex sentiment (already cited as a factor in the November 2026 sell-off) could pressure the newest and least-tested leg of the growth story

Elevated geopolitical risk (Middle East conflict/Houthi attacks on Saudi supply routes, Russia-Ukraine) remains a swing factor for both operations and the stock's 'war premium,' which appears to have partly faded already in late 2026
